signature: <Entity>Update (versioned entity): Partial<<Entity>Create> -> Partial<<Entity>Create> & { <versionField>: number | null }
justification: The generated repository reads the version in the PUT body as the version the edit was loaded at and answers 409 when the row has moved on. A versioned entity's update DTO and schema require that version, and the edit form sends the one it loaded. Unversioned entities are unaffected. docs/MIGRATION-0.x-to-1.0.md 0.9.0 carries the step.

signature: emitted list / detail / form / store / saga error display: HttpErrorResponse text and alert() -> httpErrorMessage(err, { entity, action }) from core/http-error.ts
justification: The generated handler answers a failure with a status and no body (ADR-076). Every emitted error display maps the status to a fixed sentence through core/http-error.ts and never shows the response's own text; a failed delete shows a role=alert banner (deleteError, data-testid delete-error). An app with no visible entity is unaffected. docs/MIGRATION-0.x-to-1.0.md 0.9.0 carries the step.

signature: services/<entity>.stream.ts, services/<entity>.action-streams.ts: SSE stream clients; a streaming @Action has no respond-once service method
justification: The generated kernel application serves GET {base}/stream for a realTimeApi entity and each @Action(streaming = true) as a stream only (ADR-044). A GLOBAL entity gets a client per stream route, and a streaming action has no respond-once service method, since its route answers as a stream. A tenant-partitioned entity gets no stream client. docs/MIGRATION-0.x-to-1.0.md 0.9.0 carries the step.

signature: FieldMetadata: - inList, inDetail, order, ui, dependencies; UIMetadata: - listColumns, searchFields, filterFields, formLayout, + listView, detailView, createForm, editForm, searchable, filterable, exportable
justification: The exported metadata types declare what the processor writes: every key is a component of the SDK record it mirrors, and UIMetadata carries the @UI view switches the processor extracts. The schema change alone changes no generated output. docs/MIGRATION-0.x-to-1.0.md 0.9.0 carries the step.

signature: app scaffold without a visible entity: - provideHttpClient(), proxy.conf.json, --proxy-config, environment apiUrl / apiVersion
justification: An app whose metadata declares no visible entity has no API to call, so its scaffold wires no HTTP client, dev proxy or API environment; an app with a visible entity is unaffected. docs/MIGRATION-0.x-to-1.0.md 0.9.0 carries the step.

signature: emitted package.json / styles.css: @exeris-systems/ui-kit ^0.1.0 (GitHub Packages) -> @exeris/ui-kit (npmjs); .npmrc and tailwind.config.js no longer emitted
justification: The UI kit is the public npm package @exeris/ui-kit, Tailwind v4 only (ADR-094). The emitted app depends on it and imports its theme under that name, and no file that serves GitHub Packages or a Tailwind v3 preset is emitted. docs/MIGRATION-0.x-to-1.0.md 0.9.0 carries the step.

signature: entity with @UI(listView | detailView | createForm | editForm | filterable = false): the matching component, route, link and export are not emitted
justification: The entity-level @UI view switches decide what the front emits; an app that sets no switch to false is unaffected. The Java application serves every CRUD route regardless. docs/MIGRATION-0.x-to-1.0.md 0.9.0 carries the step.

signature: SagaStepMetadata: action, compensatingAction, retries -> command, compensation, maxRetries, + service; ActionMetadata: - path, returnType, requiresAuth, + methodName, resultType, producesEvents, routeAccess; DomainEventMetadata: - displayName, payloadType, fields, + topic, aggregateType; EventSourcedMetadata: snapshotInterval -> snapshotEvery; InternalApiMetadata: - hidden
justification: The nested exported metadata types declare the keys the processor writes, so a real build's keys survive parsing, and the emitted saga state machine carries each step's compensation. docs/MIGRATION-0.x-to-1.0.md 0.9.0 carries the step.

signature: <entity>-list.component.ts: - data, filter, searchSubject, onFilterChange and the FormsModule / CommonModule / rxjs imports; typed columns, sort headers, row action buttons
justification: The list renders each column by its type and offers sort headers and row actions; paging, sorting and filtering go through the list route (ADR-096). docs/MIGRATION-0.x-to-1.0.md 0.9.0 carries the step.

signature: <entity>-detail.component.ts: Details / Related records / System sections, typed values through DatePipe, @Action buttons
justification: The detail view groups its fields in labelled sections, formats values by type, lists related records and offers the entity's actions. docs/MIGRATION-0.x-to-1.0.md 0.9.0 carries the step.

signature: <entity>-form.component.ts: Reactive Forms (FormBuilder, FormGroup, Validators, formControlName) -> Signal Forms (form, FormField, submit, FieldTree)
justification: Emitted forms are Angular Signal Forms, the shape ADR-093 fixes; selector, inputs, outputs, routes, labels, messages, classes, data-testids and the requests sent are those of the Reactive Forms version. A subclass or wrapper built on the Reactive Forms API is rewritten against the FieldTree. docs/MIGRATION-0.x-to-1.0.md 0.9.0 carries the step.

signature: @exeris/codegen-ts main / types -> exports { "./package.json" }
justification: The package's import entry point is removed: src/index.ts exports nothing and runs the CLI's program.parse() when loaded, so `import '@exeris/codegen-ts'` executed the generator instead of exposing an API. The package is a CLI; it is reached through its bin (`npx exeris-gen`), and `import '@exeris/codegen-ts'` now fails with ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED. docs/MIGRATION-0.x-to-1.0.md 0.9.0 carries the step. Released in lockstep with the tooling reactor under ADR-092.

signature: exeris-gen generate --peer (no local entity, enum or view): src/app/peers/<name>/… + app scaffold -> peers/<name>/…
justification: A run whose input has peers and no local entity, enum or view emits contracts only: the peer trees are written at the output root and no Angular scaffold (package.json, angular.json, index.html, main.ts, styles, environments) is emitted, so a consumer that is not an Angular app can import the contract types without receiving an app. A contracts-only consumer points --output at the directory that holds peers/ and imports from <output>/peers/<name>; docs/MIGRATION-0.x-to-1.0.md 0.9.0 carries the step. Runs with a local entity, enum or view are unchanged.

signature: <entity>-form.component.ts: input type by the shared field type rules; <select> only for an emitted enum; @Field(inUpdate = false) disabled in edit mode
justification: The emitted form resolves each control by the type rules the list and the detail view use. A primitive or simple-named number becomes a number input, a simple-named LocalDate / LocalDateTime a date / datetime-local input, and a java.time.Instant a text input holding the ISO-8601 value, because a datetime-local input cannot hold a value with a zone. A <select> renders only for an enum the enum module exports, so a qualified type that is not an emitted enum, which previously imported a missing symbol, is a text input. A field with @Field(inUpdate = false) is disabled while the form edits and its loaded value is sent back on update. The selector, inputs, outputs, routes, DTOs and every data-testid are unchanged; docs/MIGRATION-0.x-to-1.0.md 0.9.0 carries the step.

signature: <entity>-form.component.ts: a MANY_TO_ONE UUID foreign key is a <select> of the target's records labelled by @Relationship.displayField
justification: A foreign key whose target is generated with its service renders as a native <select> over the records the target service's findAll() returns, valued by their id and labelled by the target's displayField value (the id when the target declares no such field or the value is empty), instead of a text input holding the id. The control's id, data-testid, binding, validators and held value are unchanged, and the form injects the target's root-provided service. A value the loaded records do not contain stays an option. Without the target service the field stays a text input. docs/MIGRATION-0.x-to-1.0.md 0.9.0 carries the step.

signature: <entity>.service.ts / .store.ts / -list.component.ts / -detail.component.ts / -form.component.ts, types <Model>Filter, queries: the ADR-096 list query — server paging, sort and equality filters, no search
justification: The front's half of ADR-096: the generated list route pages, sorts and filters on the server, answers the page envelope and refuses with 400 a parameter it does not read, including search. The service's <Model>Filter and the types module's <Model>Filter hold exactly the route's equality filters (no search), <Model>SortField names its sort keys, and findAll sends sort only when set. The store reads the envelope, starts unsorted and holds its page size within 1..100; setSearch, filteredEntities and filteredCount are removed. The list reads one page through an rxResource keyed on page, size, sort and filters: the search box and the range filters are removed (data-testid search-input, filter-<field>-from/-to/-min/-max), each filter is one equality control (filter-<field>), sort headers appear only for the route's sort keys, and page sizes are 10/20/25/50/100. The query builder loses search(). The foreign-key picker requests findAll({ size: 100 }). A detail view whose ONE_TO_MANY target has a MANY_TO_ONE back lists the first ten children through findAll({ size: 10 }, { <base>Id: id }) and injects the target's service; the related-<relationship> link is unchanged. docs/MIGRATION-0.x-to-1.0.md 0.9.0 carries the step. Classified breaking under ADR-096; the output shape follows ADR-092.

signature: <entity>.service.ts / query builder <Model>SortField: - fields of an unrecognised, parameterised, array or unstorable type; <Model>Filter: + short, byte, float fields
justification: The emitted sort keys and filters are exactly the properties the list route sorts and filters on (ADR-096 Amendment 2, contract/list-query.json): Short, Byte and Float sort and filter, OffsetDateTime and ZonedDateTime sort, and a field of an unrecognised, parameterised, array or unstorable type is neither a sort key nor a filter, since the route refuses it with 400. docs/MIGRATION-0.x-to-1.0.md 0.9.0 carries the step.

signature: <entity>.service.ts, <entity>.store.ts (soft-delete entity): - restore(id); <entity>.service.ts: - throwError import
justification: Nothing on the generated server un-sets the soft-delete flag: no route, handler or repository method restores an archived row. The service and the store of a soft-delete entity keep softDelete(id) and archive(id), which call the served DELETE, and emit no restore. An entity without @SoftDelete is unaffected. docs/MIGRATION-0.x-to-1.0.md 0.10.0 carries the step.

signature: <Entity>Create, <Entity>Update, <Entity>CreateSchema: - tenantId (tenant-partitioned entity, no systemFields block); + tenantId (GLOBAL entity with a systemFields block that declares the field); local and peer DTOs
justification: The server owns a tenant-partitioned entity's owner: the generated repository stamps the bound tenant, answers 400 to another one and never updates it, and the emitted OpenAPI marks it readOnly and leaves it out of both DTOs (ADR-090). The create and update types and the create schema omit the same owner the OpenAPI does: on a tenant-partitioned entity, the systemFields.tenantIdField it names, else tenantId, with or without a block; the entity type keeps it. A GLOBAL entity has no owner, so a tenantId field it declares stays in its DTOs, including when its systemFields block names tenantIdField. docs/MIGRATION-0.x-to-1.0.md 0.10.0 carries the step.

signature: src/environments/environment.ts, environment.development.ts: - apiVersion
justification: No emitted service, store or client requests a version segment, and no generated route serves one, so the environments carry apiUrl and no apiVersion. environment.ts is written only when it is absent, so an existing app keeps the key there until it is deleted. docs/MIGRATION-0.x-to-1.0.md 0.10.0 carries the step.

signature: <entity>-form.component.ts, @Field(computed = true): - private compute<Name>() stub; computed<Name> reads the loaded entity
justification: The metadata names a computed field's dependencies and no formula, so the form computes nothing: it emits no compute<Name>() stub, whose body was a TODO and return null, and computed<Name> is this.current()?.<name> ?? null. In edit mode the read-only field shows the value the server returned; on create it is empty. The input, its data-testid, the label and the Computed from note are unchanged. docs/MIGRATION-0.x-to-1.0.md 0.10.0 carries the step.

signature: GeneratorConfig: + customBlocks (Record<customType, { import, symbol }>, default {}); pages/<view>.component.ts: CUSTOM block imports its component, binds [props]="blockProps<N>"; LIST children in <li>
justification: A CUSTOM block's element compiles only when the page imports the component behind it, so customBlocks maps each customType to the module and class the page imports and lists in its component imports; a view with a CUSTOM block whose customType has no entry, or whose props are not JSON, fails generation naming the view and the block. The block's props JSON is a blockProps<N> field of the page, bound as [props]. A LIST wraps each child in an <li>, and one <li> per row when it iterates an entity collection. A view without CUSTOM or LIST blocks is unaffected. docs/MIGRATION-0.x-to-1.0.md 0.10.0 carries the step.

signature: GeneratorConfig: + viewHeading ('title' | 'none', default 'title'); pages/<view>.component.ts: no <h1> when 'none'
justification: A page whose blocks carry their own headline, such as a HERO, got a second <h1> from the generated title heading. viewHeading 'none' omits that <h1> on every @View page and leaves the rest of the page, the route title that sets the document title, and the navigation label as 'title' emits them. The default is 'title', whose output is byte-identical to a run without the key, so no consumer has to act and MIGRATION carries no step.

signature: GeneratorConfig: + scaffold (default true); exeris-gen generate: + --no-scaffold; scaffold false: the tree at the output root, + view.routes.ts (viewRoutes), no project-root or app-shell file
justification: Additive: a new configuration key whose default keeps the old output. With scaffold false the output directory sits inside an Angular app the consumer owns, so no package.json, angular.json, tsconfig, src/main.ts, index.html, styles, environment or app shell (app.config.ts, app.component.ts, app.routes.ts) is emitted; the generated tree, its barrel index.ts and the per-view pages and routes are written at the output root, and view.routes.ts exports every view route as one viewRoutes array for the consumer's routes file. A consumer that keeps the default regenerates byte-identical output.

signature: exeris-gen generate: an existing file the previous .exeris-codegen-manifest owns is rewritten when it differs (was: every existing file skipped without --overwrite); seed files (src/index.html, src/styles.css, environment.development.ts, proxy.conf.json, .postcssrc.json join overwritable false) are kept, and released rather than deleted when no longer produced; unrecorded files and symbolic links are skipped; a missing or empty metadata directory deletes nothing (was: pruned the whole tree); .exeris-codegen-manifest: + # ownership: written
justification: The manifest records what the generator owns, and it already bounds pruning. Writing by the same rule keeps a regenerated file in step with its metadata: an owned file whose content differs is rewritten, an owned seed file (overwritable false: package.json, angular.json, the tsconfig files, .postcssrc.json, proxy.conf.json, src/main.ts, src/index.html, src/styles.css, both environments, app.config.ts, app.component.ts, app.routes.ts, core/auth.service.ts) is kept once written and released, not deleted, when no longer produced, and an existing file the manifest does not record, a symbolic link, or a path under a linked directory is neither replaced nor taken over. A manifest without the ownership line also recorded skipped files, so its entries are owned only when the file already matches, starts with the generator header (provenance line or do-not-edit notice), or is a seed. A run with no metadata deletes nothing. Default-config emitted files for a fresh directory are unchanged; the manifest gains its second header line. docs/MIGRATION-0.x-to-1.0.md 0.10.0 carries the step.

signature: exeris-gen init: + --views-only, + --app-name <name>; the written exeris-codegen.json: + scaffold
justification: Additive: two new flags, and without them init writes the configuration defaults as before, now including the scaffold key at its default, true. --views-only writes every entity generator (generateZod, generateServices, generateForms, generateLists, generateDetails, generateStores, generateSagas, generateEvents, generateTests) off and scaffold false, so generate emits the @View pages, their routes and view.routes.ts. --app-name sets appName in either preset. The keys keep the order of the defaults, so the file depends on the flags only.

signature: GeneratorConfig: + render ('csr' | 'ssg', default 'csr'); exeris-gen generate: + --render <mode>; render ssg: + src/main.server.ts, src/app/app.config.server.ts, src/app/app.routes.server.ts (seeds), angular.json + server, outputMode static, package.json + @angular/ssr, @angular/platform-server, tsconfig.app.json + src/main.server.ts, app.config.ts + provideClientHydration(); the written exeris-codegen.json: + render
justification: Additive: a new configuration key whose default keeps the old output, and init writes it at that default. With render ssg and the scaffold on, ng build prerenders to HTML each @View page whose path has no parameter or wildcard and that binds no entity, and the '' redirect as a redirect page; every other route, the entity routes included, renders in the browser through a ** Client entry, served from index.csr.html. The three server files are seeds. With scaffold false render emits nothing. A consumer that keeps the default regenerates byte-identical output.
